title: Interfacial instability as a trigger for dryout inception in two-phase CO2 flow
summary: Progress in particle physic leads to increasing in detector luminosity and a consequent increasing overheating induced by Joule effect. An effective cooling strategy is the exploitation of CO\textsubscript{2} heat latency in phase-change. An additional challenge, relevant to detectors for High Energy Particles, is the consequent geometrical constrain due to the limited space avialable for the cooling system within the detector arrangement, leading to the implementation of cooling system by means of millichannels.
